# Fingerprint — Who Learns What About You While You Open a Website

> An educational page about online privacy for people who are not technical: six steps from opening a laptop to a loaded website, and at each step, on the visitor's real data, who learns what about them and what to do about it. Everything is computed in the browser and never uploaded; only the button at step 3 sends one request to the site's own Cloudflare Worker.

## What It Does

The page is one walk of six steps: you opened your laptop (or unlocked your phone), the operating system started, you went online, you opened the browser, you typed the site's address, the site loaded. Each step shows what was measured right now from the visitor's browser, who learns it (named from the data: the makers of the system and the browser, the provider, Cloudflare, the site owner), how it works, why it matters and one thing to do, specific to the visitor's system and browser. Then the sum: who learned what, a checklist, a share text built from the data. At the bottom, the raw data for the curious.

## Key Features

- **Real data, three tiers of honesty**: rows measured right now in the browser; rows that appear after the check at step 3 (IP, provider, where the IP places you, connection type, VPN signs, TLS version, HTTP protocol, what the server got before any script); and plain explanations of what a web page cannot see (the OS maker's telemetry at boot, the DNS server's log).
- **Named parties**: Apple, Microsoft or Google for the system; Google, Apple, Mozilla, Brave, Yandex, Microsoft, Opera, Samsung, Vivaldi or The Browser Company for the browser; the provider by name after the check; the DNS server; Cloudflare; the site owner; ad networks (none on this page, 10 to 30 on a typical site).
- **One action per step**, for macOS, iOS, Windows, Android, ChromeOS and Linux, and for Chrome, Firefox, Brave and Safari.
- **Bait check for ad blockers**: three hidden elements with the class names blockers hide, plus the Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control signals; nothing is loaded from anywhere.
- **WebRTC probe** without a STUN server: it sends nothing and reports whether a real address shows in the ICE candidates.
- Russian, English and Uzbek; light, dark and high-contrast themes; share and print.

## Privacy

- **Computed in the browser**: every row of the walk, the device and OS guesses, the bait check and the WebRTC probe. The page does not upload them, and no third party sees them.
- **On page load** the page only reads aggregate stats from the site's Cloudflare Worker, which sees the IP and request headers, as any server does.
- **The button at step 3** (on click only) sends the IP to the Worker's `/api/whoami` (returned, not stored) and `/api/scan`, which asks ipquery.io (ipinfo.io as fallback) for location, ISP and connection type and Google DNS for the reverse record and the blocklists. The scan report is cached for one hour under the IP. There is no WHOIS lookup. Only if the Worker is down does the browser ask public IP services directly (ipapi.co and freeipapi.com, then ipify.org and myip.com).
- **Anonymous stats**: each check adds one to aggregate counters (browser and version, OS, country, TLS version) — no IP, no ID, no timestamps; anyone can read them at `/api/stats`.
- **Cloudflare Web Analytics** counts page views without cookies.
- **Stylesheets and fonts** (the morgunov.tech design system, IBM Plex) load from s.morgunov.tech, the author's own site, which sets no cookies and runs no analytics; those requests carry nothing about the fingerprint.

## API

The Worker answers on the site's own host, https://fprint.morgunov.tech/api/ (the older https://fingerprint-api.xfxrrpkvr5.workers.dev answers the same paths), with `/api/check` (plain text for `curl`: what a server sees about you), `/api/whoami`, `/api/scan?target=<IP or domain>` (DNS records, certificates from CT logs and security headers for a domain), `/api/stats`, `/api/health`, `/api/speedtest/*`. Rate limit: 60 requests a minute per IP.

## Languages

Russian, English and Uzbek. The page follows the browser language; https://fprint.morgunov.tech/en/ opens it in English.
